a:5:{s:39:"podlove-podcasting-plugin-for-wordpress";a:29:{s:4:"name";s:25:"Podlove Podcast Publisher";s:4:"slug";s:39:"podlove-podcasting-plugin-for-wordpress";s:7:"version";s:5:"4.4.2";s:6:"author";s:67:"<a href="https://profiles.wordpress.org/eteubert/">Eric Teubert</a>";s:14:"author_profile";s:40:"https://profiles.wordpress.org/eteubert/";s:8:"requires";s:5:"4.9.6";s:6:"tested";s:5:"6.9.4";s:12:"requires_php";s:3:"8.0";s:16:"requires_plugins";a:0:{}s:6:"rating";i:88;s:7:"ratings";a:5:{i:5;i:36;i:4;i:1;i:3;i:1;i:2;i:0;i:1;i:6;}s:11:"num_ratings";i:44;s:15:"support_threads";i:0;s:24:"support_threads_resolved";i:0;s:10:"downloaded";i:567041;s:12:"last_updated";s:21:"2026-04-04 6:06am GMT";s:5:"added";s:10:"2012-06-26";s:8:"homepage";s:46:"https://podlove.org/podlove-podcast-publisher/";s:8:"sections";a:5:{s:11:"description";s:4946:"<p>We started the Podlove Podcast Publisher project in 2012 because existing solutions were stuck in the past, complex and unwieldy. The Publisher helps you save time, worry less and provides a cutting edge listening experience for your audience.</p>
<p>Official Site: <a href="https://podlove.org/podlove-podcast-publisher" rel="nofollow ugc">podlove.org/podlove-podcast-publisher</a></p>
<h3>Getting Started Videos</h3>
<p>Starting fresh with Podlove Publisher:</p>
<p><span class="embed-youtube" style="text-align:center; display: block;"><iframe loading="lazy" class="youtube-player" width="750" height="422" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2UZrmPAcyrs?version=3&#038;rel=1&#038;showsearch=0&#038;showinfo=1&#038;iv_load_policy=1&#038;fs=1&#038;hl=en-US&#038;autohide=2&#038;wmode=transparent" allowfullscreen="true" style="border:0;" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-presentation allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"></iframe></span></p>
<p>Migrating an existing podcast to Podlove Publisher:</p>
<p><span class="embed-youtube" style="text-align:center; display: block;"><iframe loading="lazy" class="youtube-player" width="750" height="422" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/s6jL6jk6hWk?version=3&#038;rel=1&#038;showsearch=0&#038;showinfo=1&#038;iv_load_policy=1&#038;fs=1&#038;hl=en-US&#038;autohide=2&#038;wmode=transparent" allowfullscreen="true" style="border:0;" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-presentation allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"></iframe></span></p>
<h3>Compatible RSS Feeds</h3>
<p>The Publisher makes it easy to create highly expressive, efficient and super compatible podcast feeds with fine grained control over client behavior (e.g. GUID control to replace faulty episodes and for clients to reload) supporting all important meta data.</p>
<h3>Multi-Format Publishing</h3>
<p>The Publisher also makes multi-format publishing &#8211; embracing all modern and legacy audio and video codecs &#8211; a snap. By adopting simple file name conventions, the plugin allows the podcaster to provide individual feeds for certain use cases or audiences without adding work for the podcaster during the publishing process.</p>
<h3>Optimized Web Player</h3>
<p>The Publisher also comes integrated with the Podlove Web Player plugin and fully supports its advanced options including multiple audio (MP4 AAC, MP3, Vorbis, Opus) and video (MP4 H.264, WebM, Theora) format support for web browsers. This Web Player is fully HTML5 compatible and is ready for all touch based clients too.</p>
<h3>Metadata Galore</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Chapter Marks:</strong> The Publisher also makes it easy to publish chapter information in the player to make access to structured episodes even easier. Full support for linking directly to any part of your podcast on the web with instant playback included.</li>
<li><strong>Contributors:</strong> Bring your team and guests front and center. Manage contributors, including their names, avatars and web urls.</li>
<li><strong>Transcripts:</strong> WebVTT transcripts can be imported and even connected to your contributors. They are referenced in the RSS feed so they can be displayed by podcast apps.</li>
<li><strong>Seasons:</strong> Does your podcast have seasons? We got you covered with a dedicated &#8220;Seasons&#8221; module.</li>
<li><strong>Related Episodes:</strong> Manage and display related episodes on your website.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Auphonic Integration</h3>
<p>Auphonic is your all-in-one audio post production webtool to achieve a professional quality result. We provide a first class integration module for ease of use and best automation experience.</p>
<h3>Flexible Templates</h3>
<p>To round it all up, a flexible template system enables you to published Podcasts in a defined fashion and change the style at any time without having to touch your individual postings later on.</p>
<p>And this is just the beginning. We have a rich roadmap that will bring even more interesting features: integration with helpful services, much improved timeline metadata support (show notes) and much more.</p>
<h4>Further Reading</h4>
<ul>
<li><a href="http://publisher.podlove.org/" rel="nofollow ugc">Podlove Publisher</a></li>
<li><a href="http://podlove.org/" rel="nofollow ugc">Podlove Project</a></li>
<li><a href="https://community.podlove.org/" rel="nofollow ugc">Podlove Community</a></li>
<li><a href="http://docs.podlove.org/" rel="nofollow ugc">Documentation</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/podlove/podlove-publisher/issues" rel="nofollow ugc">Bug Tracker</a></li>
<li><a href="http://podlove.org/donations/" rel="nofollow ugc">Donate</a></li>
</ul>
<p>Development of the plugin is an open process. The current version is available <a href="https://github.com/podlove/podlove-publisher" rel="nofollow ugc">on GitHub</a> Feel free to contribute and to fix errors or send improvements via GitHub.</p>
<p>Requires PHP 8.0+</p>
";s:12:"installation";s:410:"<ol>
<li>Download the Podlove Publisher Plugin to your desktop.</li>
<li>If downloaded as a zip archive, extract the Plugin folder to your desktop.</li>
<li>With your FTP program, upload the Plugin folder to the wp-content/plugins folder in your WordPress directory online.</li>
<li>Go to Plugins screen and find the newly uploaded Plugin in the list.</li>
<li>Click Activate Plugin to activate it.</li>
</ol>

<dt id="is%20podlove%20podcast%20publisher%20free%3F">
Is Podlove Podcast Publisher free?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Yes! The core features of Podlove Podcast Publisher are and always will be free.</p>
</p>
<dt id="are%20there%20download%20statistics%3F">
Are there Download Statistics?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Yes! Podcast Downloads can be tracked and analyzed. You can easily see how many people downloaded you podcast episodes, which clients they used, if they prefer to subscribe to the feed or listen on your website using the web player—and much more.</p>
</p>
<dt id="are%20there%20privacy%20%2F%20gdpr%20considerations%3F">
Are there Privacy / GDPR considerations?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Podlove Publisher is GDPR compliant and provides prewritten text snippets for your privacy page. See https://docs.podlove.org/podlove-publisher/guides/dsgvo-gdpr.html</p>
</p>
<dt id="where%20can%20i%20host%20my%20podcast%20files%3F">
Where can I host my podcast files?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Any storage where you have control over the file naming is compatible with Podlove Podcast Publisher. You can manage files using a simple FTP/sFTP or use services like Amazon S3.</p>
</p>
<dt id="where%20can%20i%20ask%20questions%20and%20get%20support%3F">
Where can I ask questions and get support?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Free support where questions are answered by the community is available in the <a href="http://community.podlove.org/" rel="nofollow ugc">Podlove Community Forum</a>. There is a German community in the <a href="https://sendegate.de/" rel="nofollow ugc">Sendegate</a>.</p>
</p>
<dt id="how%20can%20i%20help%20the%20project%3F">
How can I help the project?
</h4>
<p>
<p>The continued success of Open Source project relies on the community. There are many ways you can help:<br />
Episode title in API now follows the same rules as in RSS feed. There&#8217;s a new field &#8216;title_clean&#8217; for accessing the specifically set plain episode title, but that might be null in some cases, so it&#8217;s better to default the &#8216;title&#8217; attribute to the usual rules.<br />
&#8211; If you enjoy the plugin, please <a href="https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/podlove-podcasting-plugin-for-wordpress/reviews/#new-post" rel="ugc">leave a review</a>.<br />
&#8211; You can answer questions of other fellow podcasters in the <a href="https://community.podlove.org/" rel="nofollow ugc">Podlove Community</a>.</p>
</p>
<dt id="where%20do%20i%20report%20security%20bugs%20found%20in%20this%20plugin%3F%20%3D">
Where do I report security bugs found in this plugin? =
</h4>
<p>
<p>Please report security bugs found in the source code of the Podlove Podcast Publisher plugin through the <a href="https://patchstack.com/database/vdp/9e5fb42f-70ee-4afb-9e86-886900031833" rel="nofollow ugc">Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure  Program</a>. The Patchstack team will assist you with verification, CVE assignment, and notify the developers of this plugin.</p>
<p>This product includes GeoLite2 data created by MaxMind, available from http://www.maxmind.com.</p>
</p>

<h4>4.4.0</h4>
<p><strong>Tracking &amp; Analytics</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>new: add download tracking support for Matomo (see Expert Settings &gt; Tracking)</li>
<li>new: &#8220;Recent Downloads&#8221; chart can now be added to the WordPress dashboard</li>

</ul>
<p><strong>Auphonic</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>new: Auphonic module now supports providing an API key in addition to the OAuth flow</li>
<li>new: Auphonic module now supports chapter images in the production</li>
<li>new: when re-running a production in Auphonic, Publisher now detects new files and presents a &#8220;Re-upload to PLUS&#8221; button</li>
<li>fix: switch Auphonic OAuth to the new <code>auth.podlove.org</code> service (OAuth in older Publisher versions will no longer work)</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Platform &amp; Integrations</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>new: Codeberg support as contributor social service</li>
<li>new: repair tool detects missing permission to alter tables, which prevents some database migrations from running successfully</li>
<li>new: add some situational notices that PLUS exists</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Maintenance</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>update various JavaScript dependencies</li>
</ul>
<h4>4.3.5</h4>
<ul>
<li>new: the &#8220;Repair&#8221; function in &#8220;Tools&#8221; now checks for missing database columns and adds missing ones</li>
</ul>
<h4>4.3.4</h4>
<ul>
<li>change: enable the Publisher PLUS module by default for new and existing installs</li>
<li>fix: prevent connection to PLUS service when module is deactivated</li>
<li>fix: prevent feed proxy when PLUS module is deactivated</li>
<li>fix: escape missing template id error in podlove-template shortcode</li>
<li>fix: various PHP deprecation warnings and notices</li>
</ul>
<h4>4.3.3</h4>
<ul>
<li>fix: allow selecting chapter images from the media library</li>
<li>fix: prevent media files module from hanging on new episodes without an ID</li>
<li>change: default new contributors to visible</li>
<li>fix: treat inactive episode files as nonexistent in templates</li>
</ul>
<h4>4.3.2</h4>
<ul>
<li>improve permission verification when deleting default and podcast contributions</li>
</ul>
<h4>4.3.1</h4>
<ul>
<li>add &#8220;podcast:chapters&#8221; tag to RSS feed, which Apple Podcast now prefers for chapters information.</li>
<li>change default database table character set to utf8mb4 for emoji support. For safety reasons, there is no automatic migration provided. If you prefer, you can update Publisher tables manually via SQL, but in most cases the episode table will be all you need: <code>ALTER TABLE wp_podlove_episode CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;</code></li>
</ul>
<h4>4.3.0</h4>
<p>Reworked and extended the <strong>Publisher PLUS</strong> service. It now offers the &#8220;File Storage&#8221; feature to conveniently upload media files to PLUS instead of storing it in WordPress or other external locations.</p>
<p>To get started, navigate to &#8220;Podlove &#8211; Modules&#8221;, find &#8220;Publisher PLUS&#8221; and activate it. This will add a new menu entry with further instructions.</p>
<p>There is a migration tool to copy existing media files to PLUS.</p>
<p>Give it a try if this kind of service interests you. And please do give feedback 🙂</p>
<p><strong>Other Changes</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>PLUS feature management moved: there is now a &#8220;Publisher PLUS&#8221; settings page for token management and feature toggles</li>
<li>new: media file slug &#8220;freeze&#8221;. As soon as the first media file validates, the<br />
slug is marked as &#8220;frozen&#8221; so it cannot be edited accidently any more, by<br />
automations or manual interaction. There is an edit button to consciously change<br />
it, if necessary</li>
<li>fixes &#8220;Activate for all existing Episodes&#8221; button in assets</li>
</ul>
<h4>4.2.7</h4>
<ul>
<li>security: Improved handling of image files in the download cache to block malicious uploads.</li>
</ul>
<p>Note: this should not affect normal image delivery, but please keep an eye out for any unexpected issues with cached images.</p>

<h4>4.2.0</h4>
<p>This release introduces the all-new <strong>Onboarding Assistant</strong>, enabling you to<br />
either setup a new podcast or move your existing podcast to Podlove with just<br />
your RSS Feed URL.</p>
<p>This makes it much easier for potential podcasters to get started, as it makes<br />
the initial setup process as simple and quick as possible, now only requiring<br />
the podcaster to define what&#8217;s really necessary about the podcast, without<br />
needing to worry about technical details.</p>
<p>And for the first time, you can now move any of your existing podcasts to<br />
Podlove Publisher. All you need is the RSS feed. Podlove Publisher finds all the<br />
episode data and metadata like the audio file, title, description, chapters,<br />
transcript and contributors and imports them automatically.</p>
<p>A huge Thank You goes to the <a href="https://prototypefund.de/project/podlove-publisher-onboarding-import-assistant/" rel="nofollow ugc">Prototype Fund</a><br />
for sponsoring the development of the Onboarding Assistant module.</p>
<p><strong>Other Changes</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>removes outdated &#8220;Migration Wizard&#8221;</li>
<li>generate a guid for the podcast and use it in the RSS feed <code>podcast:guid</code> tag</li>
<li>API changes:
<ul>
<li>episodes: allow filtering by <code>guid</code></li>
<li>podcast: include the following fields in responses: guid, language, feeds</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>fix: respect slashes in file slugs when urlencoding</li>
<li>security: XSS vulnerability in feed name</li>
</ul>

<h4>4.1.8</h4>
<ul>
<li>changes in an episode immediately affect the RSS feed</li>
</ul>
<p>There are various caches in place to ensure efficient delivery of the RSS feed<br />
to podcast clients. However it can be hard to guess how long it will take for a<br />
change to appear in the feed and podcatchers. Now, any change to the episode<br />
metadata or enabling/disabling an asset immediately clears the cache for that<br />
feed item, resulting in the change to be visible in the RSS feed immediately.</p>
<ul>
<li>transcripts: contributors in voices selection are sorted alphabetically</li>
<li>fix: episode license and explicit value are not emptied when saving the episode</li>
<li>maintenance: fix various notices from WordPress Plugin Check tool</li>
<li>maintenance: js dependency updates</li>
</ul>

<li>fix typo in API: <code>explicit</code> field was mistyped as <code>expicit</code></li>
</ul>

<h4>4.1.0</h4>
<p><strong>Feature: Better control over transcripts in RSS feed</strong></p>
<p>There is a new feature under <code>Podlove &gt; Podcast Feeds</code> called &#8220;Episode<br />
Transcripts&#8221; to control how episode transcripts should be referenced in your RSS<br />
feed. The default is &#8220;Publisher Generated vtt&#8221;, which is nearly the same<br />
behavior as before (In previous versions, three variants were referenced: vtt,<br />
json and srt. The json and srt URLs still work but they are not referenced in<br />
the RSS feed any more as they are not neccessary and removing them reduces feed<br />
size). There is a dedicated &#8220;Do not include in feed&#8221; option, in case you do not<br />
want the transcripts in your RSS feed.</p>
<p>Finally, you may prefer to host your transcript assets externally, just like<br />
your audio files. If you have configured a transcript asset, you can now select<br />
it in this setting. Then the RSS feed will reference this external file<br />
directly.</p>
<p><strong>Auphonic improvements</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>add button to always access the import screen</li>
<li>add button to delete a track</li>
<li>show status in production selection</li>
<li>rearrange / polish various some button and information positions</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Other</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>add: capability &#8220;podlove_manage_contributors&#8221; for contributors settings screens</li>
<li>fix: sometimes missing voices in Podlove Web Player transcripts</li>
<li>fix: sometimes an enabled asset is disabled a few moments later</li>
<li>fix: show files as &#8220;not found&#8221; when they become unreachable</li>
<li>transcripts: rename &#8220;delete&#8221; action to &#8220;clear&#8221;</li>
<li>transcripts: show timestamps in editor preview</li>
<li>upgrade heroicons (icon library) from v1 to v2</li>
</ul>

Web Player";s:4:"slug";s:18:"podlove-web-player";s:7:"version";s:5:"5.9.2";s:6:"author";s:75:"<a href="https://profiles.wordpress.org/gerritvanaaken/">gerritvanaaken</a>";s:14:"author_profile";s:46:"https://profiles.wordpress.org/gerritvanaaken/";s:8:"requires";s:5:"4.9.6";s:6:"tested";s:5:"6.8.5";s:12:"requires_php";s:3:"7.2";s:16:"requires_plugins";a:0:{}s:6:"rating";i:74;s:7:"ratings";a:5:{i:5;i:9;i:4;i:0;i:3;i:1;i:2;i:0;i:1;i:4;}s:11:"num_ratings";i:14;s:15:"support_threads";i:0;s:24:"support_threads_resolved";i:0;s:10:"downloaded";i:193599;s:12:"last_updated";s:21:"2026-01-02 2:14pm GMT";s:5:"added";s:10:"2012-07-03";s:8:"homepage";s:44:"https://docs.podlove.org/podlove-web-player/";s:8:"sections";a:5:{s:11:"description";s:2900:"<p>Podlove Web Player is a HTML5 based web player for audio and video media files that is optimized and extended for the specific needs of podcasters.<br />
It has a native integration with <a href="https://wordpress.org/plugins/podlove-podcasting-plugin-for-wordpress/" rel="ugc">Podlove Publisher</a>, can be used as a shortcode and also plays well with Gutenberg Blocks.</p>
<h3>Made for Podcasters</h3>
<ul>
<li>Podcast Chapters</li>
<li>Transcripts</li>
<li>Sharing &amp; Embedding</li>
<li>Download integrated</li>
<li>Audio Controls, including playback speed</li>
<li>Supports multiple audio file formats</li>
<li>Supports live streams</li>
</ul>
<h3>Theming &amp; Templating</h3>
<p>The Player is fully customizable in terms of</p>
<ul>
<li>Theme colors</li>
<li>Font family and weight</li>
<li>Templates and appearance</li>
</ul>
<h3>Subscribe Button Integration</h3>
<ul>
<li>Customizable Podcast Clients</li>
<li>Integration in the Player</li>
</ul>
<h3>Usage</h3>
<p>There are basically four ways to use the Podlove Web Player:</p>
<h4>1 Manual WordPress Shortcode</h4>
<p>Use a simple shortcode in your posts and pages, and the Podlove Web Player will appear, playing any media file you want to assign. Basic usage:</p>
<pre><code>[podlove-web-player
  theme="default"
  config="default"
  title="My episode title"
  subtitle="Episode Subtitle"
  poster="/files/path/to/poster.png"
  chapters="/files/path/to/chapters.json"
  transcripts="/files/path/to/transcripts.json"
  playlist="/files/path/to/playlist.json"
  src="http://mysite.com/mymedia.mp3"
  size="1337"
  show="My show title"
  duration="03:33"
]
</code></pre>
<p>Use an existing post with a media enclosure that is provided from plugins like Blubrry:</p>
<pre><code>[podlove-web-player
  theme="default"
  config="default"
  post="1234"
]
</code></pre>
<p>Or in case you have our <a href="https://wordpress.org/plugins/podlove-podcasting-plugin-for-wordpress/" rel="ugc">Podlove Publisher</a> installed:</p>
<pre><code>[podlove-web-player
  theme="default"
  config="default"
  publisher="1234"
]
</code></pre>
<h4>2 Using WordPress Gutenberg Blocks</h4>
<p>You can choose between different references, like Podlove Publisher, Blocks or you can add the meta data manually. Right now the latter option is limited to a limited set of attributes, this will be expanded in further releases.</p>
<h4>3 Automatic Integration with Podcasting Engines</h4>
<p>If you are using Podlove Publisher you should be able to select it in the Publisher Player settings.<br />
In case you are still using Blubrry you can simply enable the automatic insertions on enclosures in the settings and choose the position.</p>
<h3>Help &amp; Support</h3>
<p>If you encounter any issue with the plugin or want to request a specific feature please reach out to our <a href="https://community.podlove.org/" rel="nofollow ugc">Podlove Community</a>.</p>
";s:12:"installation";s:411:"<ol>
<li>Download the Podlove Web Player Plugin to your desktop.</li>
<li>If downloaded as a zip archive, extract the Plugin folder to your desktop.</li>
<li>With your FTP program, upload the Plugin folder to the wp-content/plugins folder in your WordPress directory online.</li>
<li>Go to Plugins screen and find the newly uploaded Plugin in the list.</li>
<li>Click Activate Plugin to activate it.</li>
</ol>

<dt id='where%20do%20i%20report%20security%20bugs%20found%20in%20this%20plugin%3F'>
Where do I report security bugs found in this plugin?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Please report security bugs found in the source code of the Podlove Web Player plugin through the <a href="https://patchstack.com/database/vdp/9e5fbc08-ca1f-4072-9764-b26c45f95853" rel="nofollow ugc">Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure  Program</a>. The Patchstack team will assist you with verification, CVE assignment, and notify the developers of this plugin.</p>
</p>

/podlove.org/donations";s:5:"icons";a:2:{s:2:"1x";s:63:"https://ps.w.org/podlove-web-player/assets/icon.svg?rev=2286308";s:3:"svg";s:63:"https://ps.w.org/podlove-web-player/assets/icon.svg?rev=2286308";}s:12:"contributors";a:1:{s:14:"gerritvanaaken";s:46:"https://profiles.wordpress.org/gerritvanaaken/";}s:6:"market";N;s:11:"custom_link";N;}s:24:"podlove-subscribe-button";a:29:{s:4:"name";s:24:"Podlove Lueken</a>";s:14:"author_profile";s:40:"https://profiles.wordpress.org/chemiker/";s:8:"requires";s:5:"3.5.0";s:6:"tested";s:6:"6.1.10";s:12:"requires_php";s:3:"5.3";s:16:"requires_plugins";a:0:{}s:6:"rating";i:100;s:7:"ratings";a:5:{i:5;i:2;i:4;i:0;i:3;i:0;i:2;i:0;i:1;i:0;}s:11:"num_ratings";i:2;s:15:"support_threads";i:0;s:24:"support_threads_resolved";i:0;s:10:"downloaded";i:61648;s:12:"last_updated";s:22:"2025-10-12 easy inclusion of the Podlove Subscribe Button. Put it in your sidebar with a simple widget or include the button in pages and/or posts with a simple shortcode.</p>
<h3>About the Podlove Subscribe Button</h3>
<p>The Podlove Subscribe Button allows for simple subscription of podcasts in anybody&#8217;s favorite podcast app right from the browser without having to deal with pesky feed URLs and go on a hunt for feed subscription dialogues.</p>
<p>The button knows how to activate the subscription functionality in all popular podcast apps supporting various operating systems including but not limited to iOS, Android, WindowsPhone, OSX, Windows and Linux.</p>
<p>The button is centrally hosted and gets permanently updated when new podcast apps emerge or when new features are added. Using the button ensures your podcast can easily be subscribed to and presents an ever more popular user interface that your audience gets more and more used to.</p>
<h3>About Podlove</h3>
<p>Podlove is an open source initiative to improve the overall podcasting infrastructure and to come up with simple but helpful standards and tools to make publishing and listening to podcast as easy as possible.</p>
<p>Podlove currently provides:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://publisher.podlove.org" rel="nofollow ugc"><strong><em>Podlove Podcast Publisher</em></strong></a> &#8211; a powerful plugin for WordPress for podcasters to publish metadata-rich podcasts</li>
<li><strong><em>Podlove Web Player</em></strong> &#8211; a podcast-optimized HTML5 web player with chapter support</li>
<li><a href="https://subscribe-button.podlove.org" rel="nofollow ugc"><strong><em>Podlove Subscribe Button</em></strong></a> &#8211; a centrally hosted universal podcast subscribe button for the web</li>
</ul>
<h3>Other Resources</h3>
<ul>
<li>Podlove Project: https://podlove.org/</li>
<li>Podlove Community: https://community.podlove.org/</li>
<li>Documentation: https://docs.podlove.org/</li>
<li>Donate: https://podlove.org/donations/</li>
</ul>
";s:12:"installation";s:4139:"<h3>Install the plugin</h3>
<ol>
<li>Upload the plugin folder to the <code>/wp-content/plugins/</code> directory</li>
<li>Activate the plugin through the &#8216;Plugins&#8217; menu in WordPress</li>
</ol>
<h3>Configure buttons</h3>
<ol>
<li>Navigate to <code>Settings &gt; Podlove Subscribe Button</code></li>
<li>Fill out all fields, save and grab the shortcode</li>
<li>Add the button to your blog using the shortcode <code>[podlove-subscribe-button id="{{yourButtonID}}"]</code> with your button ID, or use the provided Podlove Subscribe Button Widget</li>
</ol>
<h3>Display the Subscribe Button in your Sidebar using a Widget</h3>
<p>Go to <code>Appearance -&gt; Widgets</code> and drag the &#8220;Podlove Subscribe Button&#8221; widget to your sidebar configuration. Select the pre-configured button from the list and determine which style you want. That&#8217;s it. The button should show up in your sidebar. Optionally add a title and description for your widget.</p>
<p>This is the easiest and recommended way of using this plugin especially if you ony want to display a button for a single podcast. For best visibility choose size &#8220;big&#8221; and format &#8220;cover&#8221; to make your Subscribe Button stand out and easily locatable.</p>
<h3>Include the Subscribe Button in WordPress pages using a Shortcode</h3>
<p>If you want to include a Podlove Subscribe Button in a WordPress page (or a post) just put the shortcode <code>[podlove-subscribe-button]</code> at the desired position in your text. Use the following shortcode parameters to configure it properly:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>button</code> &#8211; the ID of one of your preconfigured buttons</li>
<li><code>size</code> &#8211; one of &#8216;small&#8217;, &#8216;medium&#8217;, &#8216;big&#8217;</li>
<li><code>width</code> &#8211; specify desired button width in CSS compatibles values or &#8216;auto&#8217; automatic width depending on context.</li>
<li><code>color</code> &#8211; specify the color of the button in a CSS compatible format (keyword, rgb-hex, rgb, rgba, hsl, hsla)</li>
<li><code>style</code> &#8211; default is filled, options are &#8216;outline&#8217; and &#8216;frameless&#8217;</li>
<li><code>format</code> &#8211; default is a rectangle, options are &#8216;square&#8217; and &#8216;cover&#8217; (<strong>Note</strong>: &#8216;cover&#8217; has a max size of 300px)</li>
<li><code>hide</code> &#8211; if set to <code>true</code> the button will not be shown (useful if you want to use your own element)</li>
<li><code>language</code> &#8211; specify the language the texts on the button and popup should be in (currently supports &#8216;de&#8217;, &#8216;en&#8217;, &#8216;eo&#8217;, &#8216;fi&#8217;, &#8216;fr&#8217;, &#8216;nl&#8217;, &#8216;zh&#8217; and &#8216;ja&#8217;)</li>
</ul>
<p>Note that if you do not provide one of the attributes the subscribe button will use the globally set default.</p>
<h3>Shortcode Examples</h3>
<pre><code>[podlove-subscribe-button button="mybutton1" size="big"]
</code></pre>
<p>Displays a large button with the podcast logo on top using data from button configuration with id &#8220;mybutton1&#8221;. All other options will be set to the globally set default values.</p>
<pre><code>[podlove-subscribe-button button="mybutton2" size="medium" width="100pt" language="de"]
</code></pre>
<p>Displays a small button with a width of 100pt using data from button configuration with id &#8220;mybutton2&#8221; in german. All other options will be set to the globally set default values.</p>
<pre><code>[podlove-subscribe-button button="mybutton3" size="big" width="auto" format="cover"]
</code></pre>
<p>Displays a big button with a the podcast cover and automatically adjusted using data from button configuration with id &#8220;mybutton3&#8221;. All other options will be set to the globally set default values.</p>
<pre><code>[podlove-subscribe-button button="mybutton4" format="square" style="frameless"]
</code></pre>
<p>Displays a small, frameless square button with using data from button configuration with id &#8220;mybutton4&#8221;. All other options will be set to the globally set default values.</p>
";s:3:"faq";s:2304:"
<dt id='i%27m%20running%20the%20podlove%20publisher.%20do%20i%20need%20this%20plugin%20to%20display%20a%20subscribe%20button%3F'>
I&#8217;m running the Podlove Publisher. Do I need this plugin to display a Subscribe button?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Yes and No. If you simply want to display a Subscribe Button for your Podcast you publish with the Podlove Publisher you do not need this plugin as the Publisher itself provides this functionality. If you want to display multiple Subscribe Buttons you can use the Subscribe Button plugin.</p>
</p>
<dt id='where%20do%20i%20create%20those%20%22network-wide%22%20buttons%3F'>
Where do I create those &#8220;Network-wide&#8221; Buttons?
</h4>
<p>
<p>You can find the Panel in the Networks Settings Section</p>
</p>
<dt id='does%20this%20plugin%20actually%20contain%20the%20code%20for%20the%20button%3F'>
Does this plugin actually contain the code for the button?
</h4>
<p>
<p>No. This plugin just embeds the code that is needed to display the Podlove Subscribe Button. The button itself is served live from api.podlove.org</p>
</p>
<dt id='do%20i%20update%20the%20plugin%20to%20get%20support%20for%20more%20clients%3F'>
Do I update the plugin to get support for more clients?
</h4>
<p>
<p>No. As the Podlove Subscribe Button is hosted centrally, it gets updated regularly independent from this pugin.</p>
</p>
<dt id='i%20am%20a%20podcast%20app%20developer%20and%20would%20like%20my%20app%20be%20listed%20in%20the%20button.%20what%20do%20i%20need%20to%20do%3F'>
I am a podcast app developer and would like my app be listed in the button. What do I need to do?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Consult the information provided on <a href="https://podlove.org/podlove-subscribe-button" rel="nofollow ugc">the technical information page</a> at podlove.org on how the button works and what app developers need to support and do in order to get listed in the button.</p>
</p>
<dt id='how%20can%20i%20report%20security%20bugs%3F'>
How can I report security bugs?
</h4>
<p>
<p>You can report security bugs through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program. The Patchstack team helps validate, triage and handle any security vulnerabilities. <a href="https://patchstack.com/database/vdp/54baba88-4c9c-4194-8707-5e0f37dfb763" rel="nofollow ugc">Report a security vulnerability.</a></p>
</p>

<p>The ultimate user profile &amp; membership plugin for WordPress. The plugin makes it a breeze for users to sign-up and become members of your website. The plugin allows you to add beautiful user profiles to your site and is designed for creating advanced online communities and membership sites. Lightweight and highly extendible, Ultimate Member will enable you to create almost any type of site where users can join and become members with absolute ease.</p>
<h4>Features of the plugin include:</h4>
<ul>
<li>Front-end user profiles</li>
<li>Front-end user registration</li>
<li>Front-end user login</li>
<li>Custom form fields</li>
<li>Conditional logic for form fields</li>
<li>Drag and drop form builder</li>
<li>User account page</li>
<li>Custom user roles</li>
<li>Member directories</li>
<li>User emails</li>
<li>Content restriction</li>
<li>Conditional nav menus</li>
<li>Show author posts &amp; comments on user profiles</li>
<li>Developer friendly with dozens of actions and filters</li>
</ul>
<p>Read about all of the plugin&#8217;s features at <a href="https://ultimatemember.com" rel="nofollow ugc">Ultimate Member</a></p>
<h4>Paid Extensions</h4>

<h4>Theme</h4>
<p>Our official <a href="https://ultimatemember.com/theme/" rel="nofollow ugc">theme</a> is purpose built for websites that have logged in and out users. The <a href="https://ultimatemember.com/theme/" rel="nofollow ugc">theme</a> has deep integration with Ultimate Member plugin and the extensions, different header designs for logged-in/out users and works alongside the Beaver Builder and Elementor page builders.</p>
<h4>Our other plugins</h4>
<p>In addition to Ultimate Member, we also have two other plugins: <a href="https://forumwpplugin.com/" rel="nofollow ugc">ForumWP</a> and <a href="https://wordpress.org/plugins/jobboardwp" rel="ugc">JobBoardWP</a>.</p>
<h4>ForumWP</h4>
<p><a href="https://forumwpplugin.com/" rel="nofollow ugc">ForumWP</a> is a forum plugin which adds an online forum to your website, allowing users to create topics and write replies. Forums are a great way to build and grow an online community.</p>
<h4>JobBoardWP</h4>
<p><a href="https://wordpress.org/plugins/jobboardwp" rel="ugc">JobBoardWP</a> is a job board plugin which adds a modern job board to your website. Display job listings and allow employers to submit and manage jobs all from the front-end.</p>
<h4>Development * Translations</h4>
<p>If you&#8217;re a developer and would like to contribute to the source code of the plugin you can do so via our <a href="https://github.com/ultimatemember/ultimatemember" rel="nofollow ugc">GitHub Repository</a>.</p>
<p>Want to add a new language to Ultimate Member? Great! You can contribute via <a href="https://translate.wordpress.org/projects/wp-plugins/ultimate-member" rel="nofollow ugc">translate.wordpress.org</a>.</p>
<p>If you are a developer and you need to know the list of UM Hooks, make this via our <a href="https://docs.ultimatemember.com/article/1324-hooks-list" rel="nofollow ugc">Hooks Documentation</a> or <a href="https://ultimatemember.github.io/ultimatemember/hooks/" rel="nofollow ugc">Hooks Documentation v2</a>.</p>
<p>If you are a developer and you need to know the structure of our code, make this via our <a href="https://ultimatemember.github.io/ultimatemember/phpdoc/" rel="nofollow ugc">Documentation API</a>.</p>
<h4>Documentation &amp; Support</h4>

If you can’t find a solution to your issue then you can create a topic on the <a href="https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/ultimate-member" rel="ugc">support forum</a>.</p>

";s:3:"faq";s:3302:"
<dt id="do%20i%20need%20to%20know%20any%20coding%20to%20use%20this%20plugin%3F">
Do I need to know any coding to use this plugin?
</h4>
<p>
<p>No, we have built Ultimate Member to be extremely easy to use and does not require you to manually build shortcodes or have any coding knowledge.</p>
</p>
<dt id="is%20ultimate%20member%20mobile%20responsive%3F">
Is Ultimate Member mobile responsive?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Yes. Ultimate Member is designed to adapt nicely to any screen resolution. It includes specific designs for phones, tablets and desktops.</p>
</p>
<dt id="is%20ultimate%20member%20multi-site%20compatible%3F">
Is Ultimate Member multi-site compatible?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Yes. Ultimate Member works great on both single site and multi-site WordPress installs.</p>
</p>
<dt id="does%20the%20plugin%20work%20with%20any%20wordpress%20theme%3F">
Does the plugin work with any WordPress theme?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Yes. Ultimate Member will work with any properly coded theme. However, some themes may cause conflicts with the plugin. If you find a styling issue with your theme please create a post in the community forum.</p>
</p>
<dt id="does%20the%20plugin%20work%20with%20caching%20plugins%3F">
Does the plugin work with caching plugins?
</h4>
<p>
<p>The plugin works with popular caching plugins by automatically excluding Ultimate Member pages from being cached. This ensures other visitors to a page will not see the private information of another user. However, if you add features of Ultimate Member to other pages you have to exclude those pages from being cached through your cache plugin settings panel.</p>
</p>
<dt id="does%20ultimate%20member%20restrict%20access%20to%20wp-login.php%20when%20the%20plugin%20is%20active%3F">
Does Ultimate Member restrict access to wp-login.php when the plugin is active?
</h4>
<p>
<p>The plugin does not restrict access to the wp-login.php page when active, so that our plugin does not interfere with the existing functionality of a website or other plugins that may utilise the default login page. If you wish to restrict access to the wp-login.php page you can use a plugin such as <a href="https://wordpress.org/plugins/wps-hide-login/" rel="ugc">WPS Hide Login</a> or another plugin that removes the ability to login via wp-login.php.</p>
</p>
<dt id="are%20ultimate%20member%20login%2Fregistration%20pages%20required%3F">
Are Ultimate Member Login/Registration pages required?
</h4>
<p>
<p>No, you do not need to use our plugin’s login or registration pages and can use another plugin or the default WordPress methods for user registration and login.</p>
</p>
<dt id="are%20additional%20php%20modules%20necessary%20for%20the%20plugin%20to%20work%20correctly%3F">
Are additional PHP modules necessary for the plugin to work correctly?
</h4>
<p>
<p>No specific extensions are needed. But we highly recommended keep active these PHP modules: <code>mbstring</code>, <code>json</code>, <code>dom</code>, <code>exif</code>, <code>gd</code>, <code>fileinfo</code>, <code>curl</code>, <code>iconv</code>. wp-admin &gt; Tools &gt; Site Health page has a summary about your installation and required modules. All major extensions are listed <a href="https://make.wordpress.org/hosting/handbook/server-environment/#php-extensions" rel="nofollow ugc">here</a>.</p>
</p>

<p>IMPORTANT: PLEASE UPDATE THE PLUGIN TO AT LEAST VERSION 2.6.7 IMMEDIATELY. VERSION 2.6.7 PATCHES SECURITY PRIVILEGE ESCALATION VULNERABILITY. <h4>2.11.3 2026-03-26</h4>
<p><strong>Enhancements</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Added: UM &gt; Settings &gt; Advanced &gt; APIs section for set available APIs settings.</li>
<li>Added: GoogleMaps API setting when it&#8217;s available.</li>
<li>Added: Function <code>UM()-&gt;mail()-&gt;enabled_email()</code> for checking if the email notification is enabled by the user.</li>
<li>Added: <code>color</code> type of sanitize settings saved in wp-admin.</li>
<li>Added: Checking array type of submission data when <code>url</code> type of sanitize is used in wp-admin.</li>
<li>Added: Enhance UM form sanitization filter with $form_data param. Added the $form_data parameter to the <code>um_sanitize_form_submission</code> filter.</li>
<li>Added: Option for special character requirement for passwords. It&#8217;s situated in &#8220;General &gt; Users &gt; Password requires special character&#8221; (based on @faisalahammad suggestions)</li>
<li>Added: Filter hook <code>um_before_account_delete_text</code> for changing before delete account text by 3rd-party plugins. End-customers can use it for translations.</li>
<li>Added: Filter hook <code>um_custom_{$message_key}</code> (<code>um_custom_pending_message</code>, <code>um_custom_checkmail_message</code>) for changing after-registration message based on the user status by 3rd-party plugins. End-customers can use it for translations.</li>
<li>Added: Filter hook <code>um_convert_tags_blacklist_fields</code> For 3rd-party integrations to control the usermeta keys in <code>um_convert_tags()</code> function.</li>
<li>Added: <code>.um-display-none</code> CSS utility + <code>umShow()/umHide()/umToggle()</code> jQuery helpers.</li>
<li>Added: <code>um-notice</code> JS library.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Bugfixes</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Fixed: Security issue, CVE ID: CVE-2026-4248. Added blacklist filter for convert_tag replace placeholders function.</li>
<li>Fixed: HTML sanitization logic for textarea-type custom fields with enabled HTML using setting.</li>
<li>Fixed: WP editor formatting to prevent incorrect HTML entity conversion when using html-mode in the textarea-type custom fields. Applied and removed this filter dynamically to avoid interfering with other processes.</li>
<li>Fixed: Dynamic string translation pattern and improve escaping. Replaced incorrect __(&#8216;%s&#8217;) pattern. (@faisalahammad)</li>
<li>Fixed: <code>wp_die()</code> function triggering on the frontend actions. Added UM notice above the User Profile page. (based on @faisalahammad suggestions)</li>
<li>Fixed: Password reset key handling for multiple users. Previously, the static reset key caused issues when handling password resets for multiple users simultaneously.</li>
<li>Fixed: <code>um_trim_string()</code> function for using with UTF-8 symbols.</li>
<li>Fixed: PHP Notice: Function WP_Scripts::add was called incorrectly.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Templates Requiring Update</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>members.php</li>
<li>message.php</li>
<li>restricted-blog.php</li>
<li>restricted-taxonomy.php</li>
</ul>

<li>Fixed: Typo in labels.</li>

Kit by Google &#8211; Analytics, Search Console, AdSense, Speed";s:4:"slug";s:15:"google-site-kit";s:7:"version";s:7:"1.177.0";s:6:"author";s:59:"<a href="https://profiles.wordpress.org/google/">Google</a>";s:14:"author_profile";s:38:"https://profiles.wordpress.org/google/";s:8:"requires";s:3:"5.2";s:6:"tested";s:3:"7.0";s:12:"requires_php";s:3:"7.4";s:16:"requires_plugins";a:0:{}s:6:"rating";i:84;s:7:"ratings";a:5:{i:5;i:730;i:4;i:48;i:3;i:31;i:2;i:40;i:1;i:143;}s:11:"num_ratings";i:992;s:15:"support_threads";i:59;s:24:"support_threads_resolved";i:52;s:10:"downloaded";i:252356037;s:12:"last_updated";s:21:"2026-04-21 for insights about how people find and use your site. Site Kit is the one-stop solution to deploy, manage, and get insights from critical Google tools to make the site successful on the web. It provides authoritative, up-to-date insights from multiple Google products directly on the WordPress dashboard for easy access, all for free.</p>
<h4>Bringing the best of Google tools to WordPress</h4>
<p>Site Kit includes powerful features that make using these Google products seamless and flexible:</p>
<ul>
<li>Easy-to-understand stats directly on your WordPress dashboard</li>
<li>Official stats from multiple Google tools, all in one dashboard</li>
<li>Quick setup for multiple Google tools without having to edit the source code of your site</li>
<li>Metrics for your entire site and for individual posts</li>
<li>Easy-to-manage, granular permissions across WordPress and different Google products</li>
</ul>
<h4>Supported Google tools</h4>
<p>Site Kit shows key metrics and insights from different Google products:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Search Console:</strong> Understand how Google Search discovers and displays your pages in Google Search. Track how many people saw your site in Search results, and what query they used to search for your site.</li>
<li><strong>Analytics:</strong> Explore how users navigate your site and track goals you&#8217;ve set up for your users to complete.</li>
<li><strong>AdSense:</strong> Keep track of how much your site is earning you.</li>
<li><strong>PageSpeed Insights:</strong> See how your pages perform compared to other real-world sites. Improve performance with actionable tips from PageSpeed Insights.</li>
<li><strong>Tag Manager:</strong> Use Site Kit to easily set up Tag Manager- no code editing required. Then, manage your tags in Tag Manager.</li>
<li><strong>Sign in with Google:</strong> Allows visitors to sign up and log in to your site with their existing Google account.</li>
<li><strong>Reader Revenue Manager:</strong> Helps you grow, retain, and engage your site visitors via subscription, contribution, newsletters, surveys, and custom prompts.</li>
<li><strong>Ads:</strong> Get customers and sell more with targeted traffic from Google Ads.</li>
</ul>
";s:12:"installation";s:1809:"<p><strong>Note</strong>: Make sure that your website is live. If your website isn&#8217;t live yet, Site Kit can&#8217;t show you any data.<br />
However, if you have a staging environment in addition to your production site, Site Kit can display data from your production site in the staging environment. Learn how to use <a href="https://sitekit.withgoogle.com/documentation/using-site-kit/staging/" rel="nofollow ugc">Site Kit with a staging environment</a>.</p>
<h4>Installation from within WordPress</h4>
<ol>
<li>Visit <strong>Plugins &gt; Add New</strong>.</li>
<li>Search for <strong>Site Kit by Google</strong>.</li>
<li>Install and activate the Site Kit by Google plugin.</li>
<li>Connect Site Kit to your Google account. If there are multiple WordPress admins, keep in mind that each admin must connect their own Google account in order to access the plugin.</li>
</ol>
<h4>Manual installation</h4>
<ol>
<li>Upload the entire <code>google-site-kit</code> folder to the <code>/wp-content/plugins/</code> directory.</li>
<li>Visit <strong>Plugins</strong>.</li>
<li>Activate the Site Kit by Google plugin.</li>
<li>Connect Site Kit to your Google account. If there are multiple WordPress admins, keep in mind that each admin must connect their own Google account in order to access the plugin.</li>
</ol>
<h4>After activation</h4>
<ol>
<li>Visit the new <strong>Site Kit</strong> menu.</li>
<li>Follow the instructions in the setup flow.</li>
<li>Go to the main Site Kit dashboard which already displays key metrics from Search Console.</li>
<li>Connect additional Google tools under <strong>Site Kit &gt; Settings</strong>. Learn more about <a href="https://sitekit.withgoogle.com/documentation/getting-started/connecting-services/" rel="nofollow ugc">which tools are right for you</a>.</li>
</ol>

<dt id="is%20site%20kit%20free%3F">
Is Site Kit free?
</h4>
<p>
<p>The Site Kit plugin is free and open source, and will remain so. Individual Google products included in Site Kit are subject to standard terms and fees (if any) for those products.</p>
</p>
<dt id="what%20are%20the%20minimum%20requirements%20for%20site%20kit%3F">
What are the minimum requirements for Site Kit?
</h4>
<p>
<p>In order to successfully install and use Site Kit, your site must meet the following requirements:</p>
<ul>
<li>WordPress version 5.2+</li>
<li>PHP version 7.4+</li>
<li>Modern browser – Internet Explorer is not supported</li>
<li>Is publicly accessible – it isn’t in maintenance mode, accessible only via password, or otherwise blocked</li>
<li>REST API is available – Site Kit must be able to communicate via REST API with Google services. To ensure that the REST API is available for your site, go to Tools &gt; Site Health.</li>
</ul>
</p>
<dt id="why%20is%20my%20dashboard%20showing%20%E2%80%9Cgathering%20data%E2%80%9D%20and%20none%20of%20my%20service%20data%3F">
Why is my dashboard showing “gathering data” and none of my service data?
</h4>
<p>
<p>It can take a few days after connecting Site Kit to a Google service for data to begin to display in your dashboard. The “gathering data” message typically appears when you’ve recently set up a Google service (i.e. just created a new Analytics account) and/or your site is new, and data is not yet available for display.</p>
<p>If you are still seeing this message after a few days, feel free to get in touch with us on the <a href="https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/google-site-kit/" rel="ugc">support forum</a>.</p>
</p>
<dt id="why%20aren%E2%80%99t%20any%20ads%20appearing%20on%20my%20site%20after%20i%20connected%20adsense%3F">
Why aren’t any ads appearing on my site after I connected AdSense?
</h4>
<p>
<p>If you’re new to AdSense when you connect via Site Kit, your new AdSense account and your site will need to be manually reviewed and approved for ads by the AdSense team. Ads will not display until your account and site have been approved. <a href="https://support.google.com/adsense/answer/76228" rel="nofollow ugc">Check out this guide for more information about the approval process and timeline.</a></p>
<p>You can check your approval status in Site Kit by going to <strong>Settings &gt; Connected Services &gt; AdSense</strong> and clicking <strong>Check your site status</strong>. This link will direct you to AdSense. If you see “Ready,” your account and site have been approved and should be displaying ads. If you see “Getting ready…,” your account and site are still under review and your site will not display ads until they have been approved.</p>
<p>If Site Kit has successfully added the AdSense snippet to your site and your account and site have been approved, but your site is still not showing ads, <a href="https://support.google.com/adsense/#topic=3373519" rel="nofollow ugc">contact the AdSense Help Center for assistance</a>.</p>
<p>You can find more information on how Site Kit works with AdSense in our <a href="https://sitekit.withgoogle.com/documentation/using-site-kit/managing-adsense/" rel="nofollow ugc">Managing AdSense guide</a>.</p>
</p>
<dt id="is%20site%20kit%20gdpr%20compliant%3F">
Is Site Kit GDPR compliant?
</h4>
<p>
<p>When using Site Kit, site owners are responsible for managing notice and consent requirements – including GDPR requirements – as described in <a href="https://policies.google.com/terms" rel="nofollow ugc">Google’s Terms of Service</a>.</p>
<p>By default, Site Kit does anonymize IP addresses upon activation of the Google Analytics module. This setting can be turned off in <strong>Site Kit &gt; Settings &gt; Analytics &gt; Anonymize IP addresses</strong>.</p>
<p>There are a number of third-party plugins that allow you to block Google Analytics, Tag Manager, or AdSense from capturing data until a visitor to the site consents. Some of these work natively with Site Kit by providing plugin-specific configurations. You can find out more about these by visiting our <a href="https://sitekit.withgoogle.com/documentation/using-site-kit/gdpr-compliance-and-privacy/" rel="nofollow ugc">GDPR compliance and privacy page</a>.</p>
</p>
<dt id="where%20can%20i%20get%20additional%20support%3F">
Where can I get additional support?
</h4>
<p>
<p>Please create a new topic on our <a href="https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/google-site-kit/" rel="ugc">WordPress.org support forum</a>. Be sure to follow the <a href="https://wordpress.org/support/guidelines/" rel="ugc">support forum guidelines</a> when posting.</p>
</p>
